correctness.rationale: Every limited dominating set is classified disjointly by apex selection. Apex-present sets omit at most k old vertices; apex-absent sets correspond exactly to (k-1)-limited dominating sets of the nonempty base. Forced selection of isolated vertices yields an exact recurrence for arbitrary threshold creation strings. For clique bouquets, an omitted apex contributes exactly one outside neighbor to each selected blade vertex, giving independent binomial bounds. The two branch minima and exact multiplicities, including equality, follow without asymptotics. Checks replayed: 1991 heterogeneous polynomial comparisons, 5405 universal-join comparisons, 693 uniform parameter cases, 4608 threshold-string cases. The finite checks are corroborative rather than the proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The known universal-vertex lemma covers only the k=1 minimum and is explicitly excluded from the novel claim; it cannot determine arbitrary capacity polynomials or minimum multiplicities. The Cartesian product results do not imply a join/coning recurrence. Complete multipartite graph results concern graphs with no intra-part edges; clique-bouquet blades are cliques and have no edges between blades. k-tuple total domination is not equivalent to k-limited domination on nonregular threshold graphs.

value.rationale: The exact coefficientwise count for the entire unbounded threshold-graph class supplies a polynomial-time exact counting frontier against the general fixed-k hardness. For common-apex clique bouquets it gives explicit weighted cardinality enumeration, a sharp optimizer switch, a plateau for uniform blades, an exact equality regime with two distinct optimizer families, and closed counts of every minimum set; these provide structural information not supplied by the known k=1 scalar bound or basic-graph formulas.
